001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
004import java.time.Instant;
005
006import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
007
008/**
009 * A dynamic version of {@link LogEvent}'s static "<code>of</code>" factory methods - same
010 * method shapes (level, message, ...), but {@link #timestamp()}, {@link #threadName()},
011 * {@link #threadId()} and {@link #loggerName()} are resolved through overridable methods
012 * instead of being passed in on every call/pulled from
013 * {@link Instant#now()}/{@link Thread#currentThread()} inline the way those static
014 * methods do. Those static methods are unaffected for now; this is a first step toward
015 * eventually replacing them.
016 * <p>
017 * Not being able to override thread name/thread id/timestamp is a real limitation for
018 * anything that needs deterministic events not tied to whichever real thread happens to
019 * construct them - tests especially, but possibly other reasons later. A test-specific
020 * implementation overriding those methods once gets an entire family of
021 * event-construction methods that are deterministic, rather than needing to thread fixed
022 * values through every call site.
023 * <p>
024 * Each arity of message argument has its own, distinctly-named method
025 * ({@link #eventNoArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Throwable) eventNoArg}/
026 * {@link #eventOneArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Object) eventOneArg}/
027 * {@link #eventTwoArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Object, Object) eventTwoArg}/
028 * {@link #eventArgs(Level, String, KeyValues, Object[], Throwable) eventArgs}) rather
029 * than being overloaded under one name and disambiguated only by parameter shape - this
030 * is meant to be the one place any facade implementation (SLF4J, JCL, JUL, ...) goes to
031 * build events correctly, and overload resolution across five-plus differently-shaped
032 * methods sharing a name reads confusingly at call sites once there are this many of
033 * them.
034 * <p>
035 * This holds no mutable per-instance state - implementations are expected to be immutable
036 * too. Implement it (or extend {@link #of(String)}'s returned instance's behavior by
037 * writing your own implementation) and override individual methods to customize how
038 * events get constructed.
039 *
040 * @apiNote a builder that in turn builds/configures a factory was considered but is not
041 * included (yet) - implementing this directly covers today's need (mainly tests and
042 * facade modules) with less machinery.
043 */
044public interface LogEventFactory {
045
046        /**
047         * Creates a factory bound to the given logger name, otherwise using default behavior
048         * for {@link #timestamp()}, {@link #threadName()}, {@link #threadId()} and
049         * {@link #messageFormatter()}.
050         * @param loggerName logger name every event created by the returned factory will
051         * have.
052         * @return factory.
053         */
054        public static LogEventFactory of(String loggerName) {
055                return new DefaultLogEventFactory(loggerName);
056        }
057
058        /**
059         * Name of the logger every event created by this factory will have.
060         * @return logger name.
061         */
062        String loggerName();
063
064        /**
065         * Timestamp to use for the next event created by this factory. Default is
066         * {@link Instant#now()}.
067         * @return timestamp.
068         */
069        default Instant timestamp() {
070                return Instant.now();
071        }
072
073        /**
074         * Thread name to use for the next event created by this factory. Default is
075         * {@link Thread#getName() Thread.currentThread().getName()}.
076         * @return thread name.
077         * @apiNote this maybe empty and often is if virtual threads are used.
078         */
079        default String threadName() {
080                return Thread.currentThread().getName();
081        }
082
083        /**
084         * Thread id to use for the next event created by this factory. Default is
085         * {@link Thread#threadId() Thread.currentThread().threadId()}.
086         * @return thread id.
087         */
088        default long threadId() {
089                return Thread.currentThread().threadId();
090        }
091
092        /**
093         * Key values to use for the next event created by this factory when a caller does not
094         * supply an explicit {@link KeyValues}. Default is {@link KeyValues#of()}.
095         * @return key values.
096         */
097        default KeyValues defaultKeyValues() {
098                return KeyValues.of();
099        }
100
101        /**
102         * Formatter to use for rendering a message when
103         * {@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)} is called on events created by
104         * this factory that take arguments. Default is
105         * {@link LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter#SLF4J}.
106         * @return message formatter.
107         * @apiNote a method rather than a parameter on the {@code eventXxx} methods below
108         * since this rarely changes per event - override it instead if a different formatter
109         * is needed.
110         */
111        default LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter() {
112                return LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter.SLF4J;
113        }
114
115        /**
116         * Creates a log event whose message is already formatted (no arguments). Corresponds
117         * to
118         * {@link LogEvent#of(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, Throwable)}.
119         * @param level the logging level.
120         * @param formattedMessage the unformatted message.
121         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
122         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
123         * @return event.
124         * @apiNote the message is already assumed to be formatted as no arguments are passed.
125         */
126        default LogEvent eventNoArg(Level level, @Nullable String formattedMessage, KeyValues keyValues,
127                        @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
128                return LogEvent.of(timestamp(), threadName(), threadId(), level, loggerName(), formattedMessage, keyValues,
129                                throwable);
130        }
131
132        /**
133         * Like {@link #eventNoArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Throwable)} but using
134         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()}.
135         * @param level the logging level.
136         * @param formattedMessage the unformatted message.
137         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
138         * @return event.
139         */
140        default LogEvent eventNoArg(Level level, @Nullable String formattedMessage, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
141                return eventNoArg(level, formattedMessage, defaultKeyValues(), throwable);
142        }
143
144        /**
145         * Creates a log event with a single message argument. Corresponds to
146         * {@link LogEvent#ofOneArg(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, LogMessageFormatter, Object)}.
147         * @param level the logging level.
148         * @param message the unformatted message.
149         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
150         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
151         * @return event.
152         */
153        default LogEvent eventOneArg(Level level, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues, @Nullable Object arg1) {
154                Instant timestamp = timestamp();
155                String threadName = threadName();
156                long threadId = threadId();
157                String loggerName = loggerName();
158                var messageFormatter = messageFormatter();
159                return LogEvent.ofOneArg(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
160                                messageFormatter, arg1);
161        }
162
163        /**
164         * Like {@link #eventOneArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Object)} but using
165         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()}.
166         * @param level the logging level.
167         * @param message the unformatted message.
168         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
169         * @return event.
170         */
171        default LogEvent eventOneArg(Level level, @Nullable String message, @Nullable Object arg1) {
172                return eventOneArg(level, message, defaultKeyValues(), arg1);
173        }
174
175        /**
176         * Creates a log event with two message arguments. Corresponds to
177         * {@link LogEvent#ofTwoArgs(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, LogMessageFormatter, Object, Object)}.
178         * @param level the logging level.
179         * @param message the unformatted message.
180         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
181         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
182         * @param arg2 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
183         * @return event.
184         */
185        default LogEvent eventTwoArg(Level level, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues, @Nullable Object arg1,
186                        @Nullable Object arg2) {
187                Instant timestamp = timestamp();
188                String threadName = threadName();
189                long threadId = threadId();
190                String loggerName = loggerName();
191                var messageFormatter = messageFormatter();
192                return LogEvent.ofTwoArgs(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
193                                messageFormatter, arg1, arg2);
194        }
195
196        /**
197         * Like {@link #eventTwoArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Object, Object)} but using
198         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()}.
199         * @param level the logging level.
200         * @param message the unformatted message.
201         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
202         * @param arg2 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
203         * @return event.
204         */
205        default LogEvent eventTwoArg(Level level, @Nullable String message, @Nullable Object arg1, @Nullable Object arg2) {
206                return eventTwoArg(level, message, defaultKeyValues(), arg1, arg2);
207        }
208
209        /**
210         * Creates a log event with an array of message arguments. Corresponds to
211         * {@link LogEvent#ofAll(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, Throwable, LogMessageFormatter, Object[])}.
212         * @param level the logging level.
213         * @param message the unformatted message.
214         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
215         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to
216         * {@link #messageFormatter()}. The contents maybe null elements but the array itself
217         * should not be null.
218         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
219         * @return event.
220         */
221        default LogEvent eventArgs(Level level, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues,
222                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
223                return LogEvent.ofAll(timestamp(), threadName(), threadId(), level, loggerName(), message, keyValues, throwable,
224                                messageFormatter(), args);
225        }
226
227        /**
228         * Like {@link #eventArgs(Level, String, KeyValues, Object[], Throwable)} with no
229         * throwable.
230         * @param level the logging level.
231         * @param message the unformatted message.
232         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
233         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to
234         * {@link #messageFormatter()}.
235         * @return event.
236         */
237        default LogEvent eventArgs(Level level, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues,
238                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args) {
239                return eventArgs(level, message, keyValues, args, null);
240        }
241
242        /**
243         * Like {@link #eventArgs(Level, String, KeyValues, Object[], Throwable)} but using
244         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()}.
245         * @param level the logging level.
246         * @param message the unformatted message.
247         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to
248         * {@link #messageFormatter()}.
249         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
250         * @return event.
251         */
252        default LogEvent eventArgs(Level level, @Nullable String message,
253                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
254                return eventArgs(level, message, defaultKeyValues(), args, throwable);
255        }
256
257        /**
258         * Like {@link #eventArgs(Level, String, KeyValues, Object[], Throwable)} but using
259         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()} and no throwable.
260         * @param level the logging level.
261         * @param message the unformatted message.
262         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to
263         * {@link #messageFormatter()}.
264         * @return event.
265         */
266        default LogEvent eventArgs(Level level, @Nullable String message,
267                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args) {
268                return eventArgs(level, message, defaultKeyValues(), args, null);
269        }
270
271}
272
273record DefaultLogEventFactory(String loggerName) implements LogEventFactory {
274}
